verdict.rationale: Snowflake's first-party Time Travel docs say you can query historical data that has since been updated or deleted at any point within a defined period. They also say you can restore deleted objects, either individual tables or whole container objects. Together these cover both halves of the story: point-in-time querying and recovering dropped tables. missing for 10: explicit documentation of restoring a corrupted (not dropped) table to a past state (e.g., clone-at-timestamp), details on the retention-period limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.
